name: airasia.com livery
description: Red fuselage with a white nose (to just behind the cockpit) and a white band wrapping the body ahead of the rear door; 'airasia.com' huge in white across the windows, 'Now Everyone Can Fly' small ahead of the white band. Red fin with the white 'AirAsia' script running down it; white engines with the red AirAsia disc; a Thai flag at the fin tip and by the cockpit.

logos.description: The AirAsia logo: a red disc with 'AirAsia' in white brush script across it, on the side of each white nacelle.
'AirAsia' in white script along the red sharklet.
A small Thai flag at the fin tip by the trailing edge.
A small Thai flag behind the cockpit windows with tiny 'THAI AIRASIA' under it (and 'ETOPS' on ETOPS aircraft).

titles.style: Very bold rounded lowercase, white, letters spaced, across the windows from behind the white nose to ahead of the white band (height = the i's height, the letters having no ascenders).
The slogan in small white bold sans above the windows, just ahead of the white band.
The AirAsia brush script, very large, white, turned to run down the fin from near the tip to the root (about 40 degrees), 'Air' above 'Asia'.

notes: AIQ is Thai AirAsia's ICAO code (IATA FD, callsign THAI ASIA); AirAsia India was IAD (now merged into Air India Express). Measured on HS-CBK from the right (2025) and checked against HS-CBH, HS-BBE (2025, right) and 9M-AJH from below (2024); no recent left-side Commons photo of a Thai AirAsia jet in plain colors was found, so the left side is assumed to be the mirror (positions as shares). Many AirAsia aircraft wear advertising wraps; this is the plain scheme. The fin title is turned along the fin, which the title fields can't express. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on HS-CBK (flipped, fitted to the measured A320 shape; the areas land on the photo's): 'airasia.com' runs x 0.171 to 0.557, 'Now Everyone Can Fly' 0.561 to 0.678, the fin's script turned the other way from first drawn: seen from the left it starts low at the root (fin x 0.25, its first letters running onto the fuselage) and reads UP toward the tip's trailing corner at about 49° (to fin 0.89, 0.75), about 7 m, 1.25 of the root chord, capitals about 0.26 of the fin's height; on the right side it reads down toward the nose, as HS-CBK shows (it had been drawn reading down toward the tail on the left). Heights left as drawn: the photo looks down on the aircraft and the fit tilts along the fuselage. The white areas' edges are straight from the side and stay as drawn.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation. The airasia.com scheme replaced the 'AirAsia' fuselage-title scheme from 2019; some older aircraft still carry 'AirAsia' script titles (otherwise the same red with white nose and band).
